clusters.heading: Local Handyman Services & Small Repair Jobs
clusters.answer: Yes. Ellis assesses minor repairs, assembly and fittings as a single job list. Include the items that no longer work, your Perth suburb and any deadline. We confirm the suitable work, access and quote directly with you.
scenario: Can you help with a sticking door before guests arrive?

Call Ellis and explain which door is affected and when you need it working. We check the hinges, frame and clearance rather than assume a new door is needed. Urgent attendance can be arranged from 30 minutes, subject to location, safe access and circumstances outside our control; confirm the visit time with our team.

clusters.heading: Preventative Home Maintenance & Routine Property Repairs
clusters.answer: Ellis can assess an ongoing home maintenance list and discuss which jobs need attention first. Agree the tasks, approval process and visit arrangements with our Perth team. The quote distinguishes routine maintenance from repairs needing separate specialist work.
scenario: Can I arrange maintenance while I am overseas?

Yes. Nominate the person authorised to approve the quote and the local contact who can arrange entry. Discuss completion photos and any reporting requirements before approving the work. We confirm the agreed repair list directly rather than treating access approval as permission for extra repairs.

clusters.heading: Sticking Internal Doors & Door Hinge Adjustment
clusters.answer: Ellis can inspect a door that will not close and assess the hinges, latch, frame and clearance. Tell us whether it rubs, drops or misses the latch. A local adjustment and installing a new door are different scopes; the inspection determines which is appropriate.
scenario: Can you assess a bedroom door rubbing after new carpet?

Yes. Mention the flooring change and show where the door catches. We check the clearance, hinges and door construction before proposing an adjustment. Fire-rated and security doors need their specific requirements checked; they are not treated as ordinary internal doors.

clusters.heading: Sliding Doors Hard to Open & Worn Rollers
clusters.answer: Often the rollers can be assessed separately from the door, but the track, frame and matching hardware also matter. Ellis checks what has worn and whether the panel is suitable to retain. Heavy glass panels require an appropriate handling method, not force to release a jammed door.
scenario: My apartment balcony door is jammed. What should I tell Ellis?

Tell us whether the glass panel or insect screen is stuck, whether it can close securely and if it has left the track. Include apartment access and building approval requirements. Keep clear of an unstable panel and arrange an assessment before trying to lift it.

clusters.heading: Torn Flyscreen Mesh & Flyscreen Remeshing
clusters.answer: Yes, where the frame and corners are sound, replacing mesh may be appropriate without replacing the frame. Ellis checks the mesh, frame, spline and fit before confirming the work. An ordinary flyscreen does not provide the protection of a security screen.
scenario: Can you quote for cat-damaged flyscreens before a rental inspection?

Yes. Count the damaged screens and tell us whether the frame is bent or only the mesh is torn. For a rental, confirm who can approve the work and provide access. We assess replacement mesh and fitting; completion timing is confirmed with you, not assumed from the inspection date.

clusters.heading: Sticking Timber Windows & Damaged Window Sills
clusters.answer: Ellis assesses old timber windows, including the frame, sill, moving parts and hardware. Explain whether the window sticks, leaks or no longer closes securely. Local timber and hardware repairs are considered alongside any glazing or more extensive replacement work required.
scenario: My timber window swells after rain. Can you assess the cause?

Yes. Describe when it sticks, where water appears and whether the sill feels soft. The assessment considers moisture entry as well as the moving parts. Repeatedly trimming or repainting the window without addressing moisture may not resolve the recurring fault.

clusters.heading: Cupboard Hinge Repairs, Drawer Runners & Wardrobe Tracks
clusters.answer: Yes. Ellis checks the hinge type, mounting holes and cabinet panel before quoting the repair. A compatible new hinge may be needed, or the damaged fixing area may require repair. Reusing the same stripped holes without assessing the panel can leave the door loose again.
scenario: Can you assess a wardrobe door scraping its bottom track?

Yes. Tell us whether it is a sliding door, whether it has come off the track and what catches. We inspect the rollers, guides, track and alignment before agreeing the repair. Do not force or lift a heavy or mirrored door that is unstable.

clusters.heading: Plasterboard Hole Repairs & Damaged Ceiling Cornices
clusters.answer: The price depends on the hole size, board condition, access and required finish. Ellis assesses the damage and quotes the patching and any agreed painting separately in the scope. Matching an old painted surface may require finishing beyond the patch itself.
scenario: Can you repair wall damage after a TV bracket is removed?

Yes. Tell us how many fixing holes remain and whether the plasterboard face is torn or loose. We assess backing, patching and the finish required. If you want repainting included, identify the wall area and any existing paint details before approving the quote.

clusters.heading: Damaged Timber Skirting, Architraves & Local Timber Repairs
clusters.answer: A damaged section can sometimes be replaced while retaining the rest, depending on the profile, material and available matching timber. Ellis checks the join, surrounding condition and finish. Mention moisture or soft timber so the cause is considered before a replacement is fitted.
scenario: Can you repair skirting gaps left after new flooring?

Yes. Tell us where gaps remain and whether the skirting was removed or damaged during flooring work. We assess the existing profile, floor level and required finish before agreeing repair or replacement. Painting and any additional flooring work should be identified in the quote.

clusters.heading: Scuffed Wall Touch-ups & Door Trim Repainting
clusters.answer: Ellis can assess painting required after a wall repair and confirm preparation, colour, sheen and the area to finish. A small touch-up may still show against aged paint. We explain whether finishing a larger area would give a more consistent result before you approve the work.
scenario: Can you match paint on a rental wall patch?

We assess the existing colour, sheen and surface, using paint details if available. Colour matching alone does not guarantee an invisible patch on weathered or aged paint. Confirm the approved area and required result with your property manager before arranging the finish.

clusters.heading: Flat-pack Furniture Assembly & Wardrobe Assembly
clusters.answer: The quote depends on the item type, quantity, assembly instructions, supplied parts and any anchoring required. Tell Ellis the product model and where it will be assembled. We separate furniture assembly from kitchen fitting, modifications and electrical work.
scenario: Can you assemble a bed and desk after I move house?

Yes. Tell us the number of items, product models and whether they are new kits or partly dismantled furniture. Keep instructions and supplied hardware together if available. We check room access, missing parts and assembly requirements before confirming the quote.

clusters.heading: TV Brackets, Heavy Mirror Mounting & Wall Shelving
clusters.answer: Ellis can assess bracket fitting where an existing power point is available. The TV, bracket, wall construction and fixing support must be compatible. New power points or changes to fixed electrical wiring are separate electrical work and should be included as a distinct requirement.
scenario: Can you mount a large TV on plasterboard in a rental apartment?

We first check the wall, support, product weight and bracket requirements; plasterboard alone is not an assurance of a suitable fixing. Confirm rental approval and the intended location. Tell us if new electrical work is required so it is not confused with bracket installation.

clusters.heading: Loose Curtain Rod Brackets & Roller Blind Fitting
clusters.answer: Yes. Tell Ellis the blind type, number of windows, product measurements and supplied brackets. We check the opening, clearance and mounting surface before confirming fitting. Fixed electrical connections for motorised blinds are separate from ordinary bracket installation.
scenario: Can you repair a curtain rod pulled out of plasterboard?

Yes. We inspect the fixing holes, wall support and rod weight before agreeing the repair. Replacing a screw in the same damaged hole may not solve the problem. Include the curtain and rod details so the mounting can be assessed together.

clusters.heading: Sagging Clothesline Wire & Folding Clothesline Repairs
clusters.answer: Repair may be appropriate if the frame, supports and mechanism can be retained. Ellis checks the line, brackets and moving parts before quoting restringing, hardware repair or replacement. Tell us whether the line sags, snaps or the unit no longer winds or folds.
scenario: Can you assess a wall-mounted clothesline coming loose from brickwork?

Yes. Stop using an unstable clothesline and explain which brackets have moved. We inspect the wall, anchors, frame and product requirements before agreeing repairs. Retensioning the line alone does not address a failing wall fixing.

clusters.heading: Letterbox Post Repairs & Garden Hose Reel Mounting
clusters.answer: Ellis can assess a freestanding letterbox installation, including position, support and supplied product. Tell us whether an old post must be removed. Ground conditions and buried services need checking before digging; the quote identifies the agreed installation work.
scenario: Can you mount a garden hose reel on a brick wall?

Yes. Provide the reel model and proposed position. We check the masonry, fixing points, clearance and supplied brackets before fitting. Crumbling brickwork or damaged mortar needs assessment rather than simply using a larger screw.

clusters.heading: Pet Flaps in Timber Doors & Ordinary Flyscreens
clusters.answer: Ellis assesses the door material, panel construction and product before fitting a pet door. Tell us the pet size and proposed position. Glass, security screens and fire-rated doors require their specific requirements to be checked, rather than treated as a standard timber cut-out.
scenario: Can you replace a cat flap in an ordinary flyscreen?

Yes, subject to the screen condition and a suitable product. We check the opening, frame and mesh support before confirming fitting. Explain if the screen is also a security door so its safety and security requirements can be assessed separately.

clusters.heading: Loose Towel Rails & Bathroom Accessory Fixings
clusters.answer: Ellis can assess a towel rail that pulls out, including the bracket, fixing holes and wall material. On tiled surfaces, concealed services and waterproofing need consideration before drilling. A towel rail is not a substitute for a correctly specified and supported grab rail.
scenario: Can you repair a bathroom shelf pulled off a tiled wall?

Yes. Tell us whether the tiles or brackets are damaged and whether water is appearing behind the fitting. We inspect the surface and support before agreeing new fixings. Recurring damp or loose tiles may need more investigation than replacing the shelf.

clusters.heading: Split Shower Silicone & Missing Tile Grout
clusters.answer: No. Replacing silicone only addresses the surface joint included in the work. A leaking shower may also have failed waterproofing, plumbing faults or movement beneath the tiles. Ellis assesses the symptoms before quoting resealing, regrouting or further investigation.
scenario: Can you assess black silicone around the shower base?

Yes. Explain whether there is staining only, split joints, loose tiles or damp in an adjoining room. We check the joint condition and signs of water entry before agreeing the surface repair. New silicone should not be offered as a guaranteed cure for an unidentified leak.

clusters.heading: Cracked Floor Tiles & Loose Tile Repairs
clusters.answer: A local replacement may be possible where a suitable tile is available and the surrounding floor is sound. Ellis checks why it cracked and the supporting surface before quoting. Recurring cracks, movement or moisture should be investigated instead of repeatedly replacing a tile.
scenario: Can you assess a loose splashback tile behind the sink?

Yes. Tell us whether the tile has moved, grout is missing or the wall is damp. We inspect the tile and backing before agreeing a local repair. Leaking plumbing or damaged backing must be considered separately from the visible tile finish.

clusters.heading: Loose Fence Palings, Damaged Panels & Sagging Gates
clusters.answer: A damaged section may be repairable if the remaining posts and rails provide suitable support. Ellis assesses the fence material, damage and access before quoting local replacement or a broader repair. Confirm approval arrangements for a shared boundary before work proceeds.
scenario: Can you repair a side gate that will not latch after rain?

Yes. We check the gate, hinges, latch and supporting posts to identify what has moved. Adjusting the latch alone may not correct a dropping frame or post. Pool gates and powered gates have separate safety requirements and are not treated as ordinary side gates.

clusters.heading: Loose Decking Boards & Deck Timber Maintenance
clusters.answer: A few boards may be replaceable where the supporting structure is sound and suitable matching timber is available. Ellis inspects boards, fixings and supports before agreeing repairs. Movement, sagging or extensive rot calls for a broader assessment rather than surface maintenance alone.
scenario: Can you assess deck screws lifting in an outdoor entertaining area?

Yes. Avoid the affected area if it is unstable and tell us where boards or fixings have moved. We check the timber and support as well as the screws. Oiling is agreed only after any required repair and preparation are identified.

clusters.heading: Damaged Patio Trim & Loose Eaves Linings
clusters.answer: Ellis can assess local pergola repairs, separating trim and lining work from damaged supports or structural movement. Describe loose timber, sagging components or recurring water damage. The assessment establishes the material and suitable work before any repair is approved.
scenario: Can you assess damaged eaves sheets on an older house?

Yes. Tell us the building age and visible damage without disturbing the sheets. The material needs identification before drilling, sanding or removal, because older linings may contain asbestos. We confirm the safe assessment and work required rather than assume a simple patch.

clusters.heading: Blocked Gutter Cleaning & Overflowing Gutter Assessment
clusters.answer: Ellis assesses gutter cleaning on single-storey homes, checking safe access and the gutter condition before confirming the work. Tell us about leaf build-up, overflow and affected downpipes. Cleaning and repairing damaged drainage components are distinct items in the quote.
scenario: Why is the gutter above my front door still overflowing after cleaning?

A blockage elsewhere, gutter fall, outlet size or damaged components may be involved. Tell Ellis where overflow occurs and what was cleaned. We inspect the drainage path and identify the repair required rather than assume more leaf removal will solve it.

clusters.heading: Patio Paving Cleaning & Small Outdoor Maintenance Jobs
clusters.answer: Ellis can assess cleaning for a small patio, choosing a method suited to the paving, joints, coatings and drainage. Describe the surface and stains. Fragile materials or suspected hazardous materials require assessment before pressure cleaning is considered.
scenario: Can paving cleaning be combined with a rental courtyard tidy-up?

Discuss both tasks with Ellis and identify the paving, garden waste and small repairs involved. We confirm what can be grouped and which work needs a separate service. Waste removal and any disposal charges should be included explicitly in the quote.

clusters.heading: Rental Maintenance & Vacate Repair Lists
clusters.answer: Yes. Provide the authorised property contact and agreed access arrangements when booking. Ellis confirms the repair scope and quote with the person who can approve the work. Changes or additional repairs need approval; permission to enter is not approval for every task.
scenario: Can you quote for wall holes, torn flyscreens and a damaged cupboard before moving out?

Yes. List the affected items and confirm which repairs the landlord or property manager has authorised. We assess patching, screens and cabinet hardware as defined tasks and agree timing directly with you. Repair work does not determine whether your bond will be returned.

clusters.heading: Pre-sale Repair Checklists & Cosmetic House Repairs
clusters.answer: Start with faults affecting use, such as doors that will not close, loose fittings and damaged trim, then discuss the required finish. Ellis can assess the repair list before photography or an open home. Underlying defects should be identified, not concealed by cosmetic work.
scenario: Can you assess doors, skirting and wall marks before real-estate photography?

Yes. Explain the deadline and which items you want retained, repaired or refinished. We inspect the faults and agree the scope and appointment with you. Cosmetic preparation is not a promise of a sale price, faster sale or a defect-free inspection.

clusters.heading: Strata Minor Repairs, Office Repairs & Shop Fittings
clusters.answer: Ellis can assess approved strata maintenance after the authorised contact confirms the work and access. Specify whether the item is within a lot or on common property. Fire doors, electrical systems and other specialist components require the appropriate assessment, not a general repair assumption.
scenario: Can you assemble office desks and hang whiteboards outside trading hours?

Tell Ellis the products, quantities, mounting locations and preferred access window. We check the fixing surfaces and confirm the booking directly. Include parking, building access and the person who can approve work; after-hours access does not remove noise or building restrictions.

clusters.heading: Home Safety Maintenance & Grab Rail Fixing Assessment
clusters.answer: Yes. A family member can arrange a household repair enquiry, nominate the person who approves work and discuss suitable access with Ellis. For grab rails, supply an existing placement plan if available. Funding eligibility and approval are separate from our assessment of the repair.
scenario: Can you assess a loose handrail at the front steps?

Yes. Explain where it moves and whether it is needed for support. Avoid relying on an unstable rail. We assess the rail, supporting material and fixing requirements before agreeing repairs; a towel rail or improvised fitting is not a suitable substitute.

clusters.heading: Itemised Handyman Quotes & Minimum-charge Questions
clusters.answer: The cost depends on the agreed task, materials, access and any separate trade work. Ellis provides a written quote after assessment. Ask us to confirm whether the work is priced by time or by the job and whether attendance, assessment or minimum charges apply before approval.
scenario: Can I request a labour-only quote using materials I supply?

Yes. Tell Ellis exactly what you will supply, including product models and quantities. We check whether the parts suit the job and identify any missing materials. The written scope should distinguish supplied items, labour, disposal and any additional charges before work starts.

clusters.heading: TV Bracket Fitting & Separate Electrical Work
clusters.answer: Replacing a tap should not be assumed to fall within ordinary handyman work. Describe the plumbing task to Ellis so the appropriate plumbing requirements and work can be confirmed. A business using the word handyman does not by itself establish a trade licence.
scenario: Does TV bracket fitting include a new power point?

No. Bracket fitting and installing or changing a power point are distinct scopes. Tell Ellis both requirements so the electrical work is assessed and quoted appropriately. Do not alter fixed wiring or ask for it to be treated as a simple wall-mounting task.

clusters.heading: Failed Shower Waterproofing & Balcony Leak Assessment
clusters.answer: Tile removal and waterproofing repairs may be needed where assessment identifies failure beneath the surface. New silicone cannot establish that the underlying membrane is sound. Ellis confirms the investigation, repair sequence and scope before quoting the work.
scenario: Can you assess a shower leaking into the adjoining bedroom?

Yes. Describe where damp appears, when it occurs and whether previous resealing helped. The assessment considers plumbing, joints and the tiled wet-area system. Surface resealing, waterproofing and retiling are distinct works; the cause should be established before choosing the repair.

guides.title: Cupboard Hinges & Drawer Runners: Repair or Replace?
guides.description: Understand loose cupboard hinges, dropped cabinet doors and drawers off their runners before arranging a repair assessment with Ellis Perth.
guides.intro: A dropped cupboard door or drawer that will not close does not automatically require a new kitchen. Identifying the moving part and its fixing surface helps distinguish a hardware repair from damaged cabinetry.
sections: Cupboard hinge pulled out: check the panel as well as the hinge

A hinge can be sound while its screws no longer hold in a damaged cabinet panel. Conversely, a worn hinge may need compatible replacement hardware even where the panel is intact. Note whether the door has dropped, a hinge is broken or screws have pulled out. Repeatedly tightening a loose screw does not establish that the fixing area can support the door. If the door is hanging unevenly, stop using it until it can be assessed safely.
Cabinet door alignment and matching hardware

A gap or rubbing edge can involve hinge adjustment, loose mounting plates or movement in the cabinet. The hinge type, opening angle and existing mounting arrangement matter when selecting a replacement. Keep the old hardware available and record which doors are affected. Repair assessment should include neighbouring panels and the closing action, not just the visible gap. A new fitted cabinet is a different project from retaining a door and repairing its hardware.
Drawer off its runners: identify what has moved

A sticking drawer may have damaged runners, loose screws, an obstruction or distortion in the drawer box. Soft-close runners are not interchangeable simply because they look similar. Width, length, load requirements and the mounting arrangement affect compatibility. Empty an unstable drawer and avoid forcing it. Explain whether the problem began after loading, moving furniture or previous work so the assessment can consider the surrounding cabinet.
What to include in a cabinet repair enquiry

List the doors and drawers affected, what they do when used and whether you want the existing cabinetry retained. Photos of the front and safely accessible hardware can help, but are optional. Include missing parts and any rental approval requirements. A useful quote identifies hardware, fixing-area repair, alignment and any finish work. Ask what changes if hidden panel damage is found before additional work proceeds.
qa: Why do cupboard hinge screws keep coming loose?

The fixing hole, panel or mounting plate may be damaged, or the door load may be affecting the fixing. Repeated tightening does not identify the cause. An assessment checks both the hardware and the material holding it.
Can new drawer runners fit an older cabinet?
Sometimes, but dimensions, clearances and the mounting arrangement must match. The drawer box and cabinet condition also matter. A compatible product should be confirmed before replacement is agreed.
Should I replace the hinge or repair the cabinet panel?
That depends on which part has failed. A sound hinge in a damaged panel needs a different repair from a broken hinge on sound cabinetry. Ellis checks both before quoting.

guides.title: Sticking Doors & Timber Windows: What Needs Repair?
guides.description: Learn what rubbing doors, swollen timber windows and dragging sliding panels can indicate, and what to include in a Perth repair enquiry.
guides.intro: A door or window that catches may need hardware adjustment, a local timber repair or attention to moisture and movement. The place it catches and when the problem occurs are more useful than guessing which part to replace.
sections: Sticking internal doors and hinge adjustment

A door that rubs after new carpet needs a different assessment from one that has dropped on loose hinges. Record where contact occurs, whether the latch lines up and what recently changed. The frame, hinges, door construction and floor clearance all affect the proposed repair. Do not assume trimming is appropriate for every door. Security and fire-rated components have specific requirements that must be checked before modification.
Timber windows swelling after wet weather

If a window becomes difficult to close after rain, describe the timing and any visible damp, cracked finish or soft timber. Moisture entry may affect the sill, frame or surrounding materials. Planing or repainting without assessing the cause may leave the same fault recurring. Hardware, sash movement and glazing can involve different repair scopes. Do not force a swollen or unstable window simply to make it shut.
Sliding doors hard to open: rollers, track and alignment

Dragging can come from worn rollers, track damage, debris or misalignment. Identify whether the affected panel is glass or an insect screen and whether it has left its track. Roller replacement does not necessarily require replacing the whole door, but compatible hardware and a serviceable track matter. Heavy glass and mirrored panels require appropriate handling. Keep clear of unstable panels rather than lifting or forcing them yourself.
Repair, replacement and access details

Tell Ellis the door or window type, the symptoms, how long the fault has been present and what you want retained. Existing photos are useful but not required. Include apartment lifts, parking, building access and the person authorised to approve work. A written quote should distinguish adjustments, replacement hardware, timber work, glazing and finishing. Repeated moisture or movement needs to be considered before choosing a cosmetic repair.
qa: Why does a timber door stick in wet weather?
Moisture can affect timber and its finish, but hinge or frame problems may also be involved. Note when it sticks and where it rubs. Assessment should consider the cause before trimming or repainting.
Does a damaged sliding-door track always need replacement?
Not always. The extent of damage, panel alignment and available compatible components determine whether local repair or replacement is appropriate. Roller work alone may not correct a damaged track.
Should I call a handyman, carpenter or glazier for a window repair?
Describe the fault rather than choosing a trade from the window name alone. Timber, hardware and glass can need different capabilities. Ellis confirms the appropriate work after reviewing the issue.

guides.title: Wall Patching & Paint Touch-ups: Planning the Finish
guides.description: Understand plasterboard holes, visible wall patches and paint colour differences before arranging patching and finishing in Perth.
guides.intro: Repairing a hole and matching the finish are related but separate tasks. Knowing the damaged material, cause and finish you want helps make the quote clear before work starts.
sections: Plasterboard hole repairs and backing condition

A door-handle hole or damage after removing a TV bracket can affect the board face, backing or a larger area than the visible opening. Record the number and approximate size of damaged areas. The repair method depends on the surrounding board and support, not only the hole diameter. Avoid opening walls to investigate concealed services yourself. On older or unidentified materials, the material should be assessed before cutting or sanding.
Why wall patches show through paint

A patched area can differ in texture, absorption, flatness or sheen from the surrounding surface. Paint colour is only one part of the finish. Preparation and finishing over a larger area may be needed for a consistent appearance. Ask whether the quote covers patching alone, preparation, priming and a local touch-up, or repainting the wall. This avoids assuming a small patch includes an invisible match across aged paint.
Scuffed wall touch-ups and aged paint

Keep existing paint details if available, including colour and sheen. A fresh coating can look different where the old finish has faded, worn or been cleaned unevenly. Small touch-ups and full-wall repainting have different material and labour requirements. Explain the result you expect, particularly before rental handover or photography. The assessment should establish a realistic finish rather than guarantee that every repair will be invisible.
Moisture, ceiling cracks and recurring damage

A stained ceiling or recurring crack is not automatically a cosmetic patching task. Report active leaks, movement, sagging and previous repairs before agreeing a finish. The cause and condition need assessment before damaged surfaces are closed or painted. Keep clear of an unstable ceiling. If a leak has been repaired, tell Ellis when it was fixed so the affected materials can be checked before finishing is planned.
qa: What is the difference between plaster and plasterboard repairs?

The materials and supporting construction differ, so preparation and patching are not interchangeable. Describe the damage and let the assessment identify the surface rather than assuming all walls need the same patch.
Why does touch-up paint look different from the rest of the wall?
Colour, sheen, age, texture and preparation can all affect the appearance. Matching a colour name alone does not guarantee a match. Discuss whether a larger finishing area is appropriate.
Should a water-damaged ceiling be dry before repair?

The water source and material condition should be assessed before patching and finishing. Active leaks, weakened board or sagging need attention; painting over a stain does not resolve the underlying problem.

guides.title: Shower Silicone, Grout & Waterproofing: The Difference
guides.description: Understand surface resealing, regrouting and deeper shower waterproofing repairs before choosing a repair for recurring leaks.
guides.intro: A leaking shower does not always need the same repair. Surface silicone, grout, plumbing and the waterproofing beneath tiles perform different roles; the symptoms should guide assessment rather than a single advertised treatment.
sections: Split shower silicone and surface joints

Silicone is commonly used at movement joints and changes of plane in a tiled wet area. A split or deteriorated joint may need surface resealing, but its appearance does not establish the condition of the system behind the tiles. Describe staining, gaps and whether the shower leaks during use. New silicone should not be presented as a guaranteed cure for a leak whose source has not been identified.
Missing tile grout and loose tiles

Grout fills joints between tiles, while the underlying waterproofing is a separate part of the construction. Missing grout, loose tiles or recurring cracking may need more investigation than refilling visible gaps. Note whether tiles have moved and whether damp appears outside the shower. Tell Ellis about previous regrouting or resealing and whether it changed the symptoms. Movement and backing condition affect the appropriate work.
Failed shower waterproofing and adjoining-room damp

Water appearing in a bedroom or below a tiled balcony may come from several sources. Plumbing, drainage, surface joints and the underlying wet-area system should be considered during assessment. Where deeper failure is identified, investigation and repairs may involve tile removal, substrate work, waterproofing and retiling. Those are distinct from surface maintenance and need an agreed scope; the visible stain alone cannot determine the complete repair.
What to ask before accepting a shower repair quote

Explain where water appears, when it happens and which repairs have already been attempted. Ask what has been assessed, what remains unknown and which surface or underlying work is included. Confirm how additional damage will be reported and approved. For apartments, include affected neighbouring areas and access arrangements. Avoid treating a maintenance quote as proof that every concealed component is sound.
qa: What is the difference between grout and silicone?

Grout and silicone serve different joint requirements in a tiled finish. Neither is a substitute for assessing the waterproofing beneath the tiles. The appropriate material and repair depend on the joint and condition.
How is resealing different from waterproofing a shower?

Resealing addresses specified surface joints. Waterproofing repairs address the underlying wet-area system and may involve removing and reinstating finishes. The required work follows assessment of the leak.
Why does a shower still leak after new silicone?

The leak may involve another joint, plumbing, movement or the underlying waterproofing. Report what was resealed and where damp persists. Repeating the same surface treatment without assessment may leave the cause unresolved.
